comparisons.peer_topic: CECL Deferral Impact on Capital Ratios
comparisons.peer_summary: The company elected to defer the effect of CECL adoption on capital amounts and ratios over a five-year period, with impacts phasing in at 25% from 2022, 75% from 2024, and fully phased in by January 1, 2025.
comparisons.comparison: BAC and MS both describe the regulatory framework allowing a five-year transition period for the CECL adoption impact on capital calculations. BAC states that TLAC ratios are calculated using the rule allowing this transition. MS explicitly details the election to defer the effect of CECL adoption over a five-year period, with impacts phasing in at 75% from January 1, 2024, and fully phased in by January 1, 2025. This confirms that both companies were operating under the same CECL transition provision mechanics during the fiscal year 2024 period.

sentences.text: (1)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, TLAC ratios are calculated using the regulatory capital rule that allows a five-year transition period related to the adoption of the CECL accounting standard on January 1, 2020.

Beginning on January 1, 2020, we elected to defer the effect of the adoption of CECL on our risk-based and leverage-based capital amounts and ratios, as well as our RWA, adjusted average assets and supplementary leverage exposure calculations, over a five-year transition period.
The deferral impacts began to phase in at 25% per year from January 1, 2022 and were phased-in at 75% from January 1, 2024.
